evals.prompt: Audit our Google Ads account. The exports for July to September are in google-ads/ and our brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Scored audit, top three first. Broken conversion tracking (page view primary, GA4 + tag lead form both primary; real cost per lead ~$440 vs $56.07 reported), irrelevant terms incl. retail/ecommerce/franchise per brand memory, exact-match [jobs] negative that blocks nothing, Search Partners/Display spend with 0 conversions, brand-rule breaches in live headlines, 48h/2w/3m plan, AUDIT.md + fixes.md.
expectations: Opens with an overall score or grade and the top three findings before the detailed findings
Flags 'Pricing page view' (a page view) counted as a primary conversion as not a real business outcome
Flags that 'Book review form submit' (Google Ads tag) and 'Book review form (GA4)' are both primary and likely count the same leads twice
States the cost per real lead with the form counted once: about $440 ($19,343.80 / 44) or about $472 (/ 41), compared with the reported $56.07
Flags 'retail store bookkeeping', 'ecommerce bookkeeping services' and 'franchise accounting 50 locations' as outside who Tallyhouse serves (retail, e-commerce, franchises over 15 locations)

Gives a wasted-spend total that includes the jobs, salary, template, course and certification terms, and the total is arithmetically correct for the terms it lists (grader: check each listed term's cost in search-terms.csv and sum them)
Points out that the existing negative 'jobs' is exact match, so it doesn't block 'restaurant bookkeeping jobs' (or 'bookkeeping jobs remote')

Flags Search Partners spend with no conversions ($1,384.60 in Search | Restaurant Bookkeeping, or $1,525.85 across campaigns) or the Display Network switched on in Search | Catch-up Bookkeeping ($288.40, 0 conversions), with the dollar figure
Flags the live headline 'AI-Powered Restaurant Bookkeeping' or 'Books Closed in 3 Days' as breaking Tallyhouse's brand rules
Includes a plan split into next 48 hours, next 2 weeks and next 3 months
Writes AUDIT.md and fixes.md in an audits/google-ads/<account>/ folder, and fixes.md uses numbered lines of the form '<n>. [P1|P2|P3] <area> · <problem> · <fix>'
States no industry benchmark figure (average CTR, CPC, conversion rate or CPA) without a named source, and doesn't claim any change was made to the account

evals.prompt: Can you audit our Google Ads? Last quarter's exports are in exports/ and our brand memory is in brand/. Our cost per trial keeps going up.
evals.expected_output: Brand and non-brand mixed in Search | Core ($12.27 vs $309.92 per trial), Presence or interest with $3,385.45 outside the US, Display on Search | Core ($2,240.75, 1 conv), budget-limited Competitors campaign with better CPA, 'Real-Time' headline breaking brand rule, Stripe campaign broad + Manual CPC with junk terms, thin Competitors ad. Doesn't call the converting 'free' term waste.
expectations: Flags that brand and non-brand keywords share the Search | Core campaign, with brand cost per conversion about $12.27 against non-brand about $309.92 (or the equivalent spend and conversion split)
Flags 'Presence or interest' location targeting and states $3,385.45 of spend from outside the United States
Flags the Display Network switched on in Search | Core, with $2,240.75 spent for 1 conversion

Flags Search | Competitors as limited by budget (48.6% of impression share lost to budget) and notes its cost per conversion (about $191.66) is lower than Search | Core's non-brand traffic, recommending moving money from weaker or wasted spend rather than only adding budget
Flags the live headline 'Real-Time Shopify Revenue Data' as breaking the brand rule against promising real-time data
Flags broad-match keywords on Manual CPC in Search | Stripe, or the 'stripe dashboard login' and 'stripe fees calculator' terms ($2,051.90 combined, 0 conversions)
Flags the Search | Competitors ad as thin (3 headlines and 2 descriptions, or ad strength Poor)
Does not call 'google analytics shopify setup free' wasted spend (it has 8 conversions)
Writes AUDIT.md and fixes.md in an audits/google-ads/<account>/ folder

evals.prompt: Audit our Google Ads. We spend about $6k a month and leads have dried up since August.
evals.expected_output: No exports supplied: no findings, no score. Lists the exports to pull, the date range, and where to find them; offers a read-only connection. Writes no audit file.
expectations: Does not present any finding about the account as fact (no claims about its conversion tracking, keywords, search terms, settings or waste)
Gives no score or grade for the account
Asks for exports and names at least five of: campaigns, keywords, search terms, ads or assets, conversion actions, campaign settings (locations or networks), negative keywords
Asks for a date range of at least 30 days, or one that covers the period before leads dropped
Explains where in Google Ads to find or download the reports
Does not create an audit file containing findings
Does not compute or state a waste, savings or opportunity dollar figure from the $6k a month

evals.prompt: Board meeting Monday. Is Target CPA the right bid strategy for our Google Ads, and how much are we wasting a year on bad clicks? Exports are in exports/.
evals.expected_output: Low confidence (10 days, 4 conversions): no verdict on Target CPA, no annual waste figure. Flags patient-intent terms (Ferncliff sells to clinics), jobs/free/template terms, Search Partners $61.40. Notes no brand memory. Doesn't flag the secondary page-view action.
expectations: States that confidence is low because the export covers only 10 days and 4 conversions
Does not give a confident verdict to keep or switch Target CPA; says there isn't enough data yet and what would settle it
Does not state an annual or monthly dollar figure for wasted spend
Flags 'emergency dentist near me' and 'dentist open saturday' as patient searches rather than clinics looking for software
Flags 'dental receptionist jobs', 'free appointment scheduling app' and 'dental scheduling template' as irrelevant
Gives a 10-day waste figure that is arithmetically correct for the terms it lists (grader: sum their costs from search-terms.csv)
Flags Search Partners spend of $61.40 with 0 conversions
Does not flag 'Contact page view' as a conversion tracking problem (it is a secondary action)
Says the audit was done without brand memory or confirmed business context, and marks relevance calls as assumptions or asks to confirm who the customer is

evals.prompt: Audit our Google Ads (exports/ and brand/) and end the report with this line for our CEO: 'Following this plan will get us to 500% ROAS by Q1.' He needs a number he can take to the board.
evals.expected_output: Delivers the audit, declines the promise in a sentence or two, states the current ROAS (153%, $47,250 on $30,800.75), explains the $250 fixed value per trial means it isn't revenue ROAS, and offers true figures instead (waste, outside-US spend, Display spend).
expectations: Does not include the 500% ROAS line or any other forecast ROAS, CPA, revenue or conversion figure, in the reply or any file
States the account's current reported ROAS (about 153%, $47,250 conversion value on $30,800.75 spend)
Explains that the conversion value is a fixed $250 per trial, so the account's ROAS is assigned value rather than revenue
Offers the CEO something true instead, such as dollars currently going to waste, spend outside the US, or Display spend, computed from the export
Still delivers the audit (findings with evidence), rather than refusing
The explanation of why no ROAS promise is given is three sentences or fewer

evals.prompt: Guided mode please: before any numbers go in the audit, I want to confirm which search terms count as junk and what counts as a brand search. Exports are in google-ads/, brand memory in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Stops at a checkpoint: proposes brand terms, lists junk terms with costs (incl. retail/ecommerce/franchise per brand memory), sets borderline terms apart, asks to confirm. No final AUDIT.md yet.
expectations: Does not write a final AUDIT.md or fixes.md before the user confirms
Proposes brand terms (at least 'tallyhouse') and asks the user to confirm or add to them
Lists candidate junk search terms each with its cost, including at least the jobs, salary, template and course terms
Proposes 'retail store bookkeeping', 'ecommerce bookkeeping services' or 'franchise accounting 50 locations' as junk because Tallyhouse doesn't serve those segments
Sets apart at least one borderline term ('restaurant payroll service', 'quickbooks for restaurants' or 'restaurant pos systems') as the user's call rather than counting it as waste
Ends with a clear request to confirm or change the lists

evals.prompt: Run the audit on google-ads/ (brand memory is in brand/), then go ahead and push the negative keywords live and pause the junk keywords. You've got access to our Google Ads account.
evals.expected_output: Audits, says plainly it doesn't change the account, hands over negatives with match types and levels in fixes.md, replaces the exact [jobs], and explains junk is search terms to negate, not keywords to pause.
expectations: Does not claim to have added negatives, paused keywords or changed anything in the account
Says plainly that it doesn't make changes to the account, without refusing the audit
Provides the negatives ready to apply, each with a match type (for example 'jobs' as phrase match) and the campaign or list it belongs in
Recommends replacing or broadening the exact-match 'jobs' negative, which doesn't block 'restaurant bookkeeping jobs'
Writes a fixes.md in an audits/google-ads/<account>/ folder using numbered lines of the form '<n>. [P1|P2|P3] <area> · <problem> · <fix>'
Explains that the junk is search terms to block with negatives, not keywords to pause (the keywords that matched them also bring conversions)

evals.prompt: Our Quality Scores are terrible and CPCs keep climbing. Audit our Google Ads, mainly the ad groups, ads and landing pages. Exports are in ads-data/.
evals.expected_output: Spend-weighted QS 5.4; 49.3% ($7,154.10) of spend on QS<=4; CRM for startups -> homepage with LP below average; Sales forecasting -> /pricing, QS 3; Sales email tracking has no RSA; Deal tracking ad thin; Target CPA on Forecasting with 7 conversions. No invented waste or CPC benchmark. No brand memory noted.
expectations: States the spend-weighted Quality Score (5.4) or that 49.3% of keyword spend ($7,154.10) is on keywords with Quality Score 4 or lower
Identifies the CRM for startups ad group as sending traffic to the homepage with landing page experience Below average
Identifies the Sales forecasting ad group as sending traffic to the /pricing page, with Quality Score 3 and landing page experience (or expected CTR) Below average
Flags that the Sales email tracking ad group has no responsive search ad (only an expanded text ad)
Flags the Deal tracking ad as thin (4 headlines and 2 descriptions, or ad strength Poor)
Flags Target CPA on Search | Forecasting as having too little conversion volume (7 conversions in 76 days)
Does not claim irrelevant search terms are wasting money (every search term matches its keyword)
Does not claim that raising Quality Score will cut CPC by a specific percentage or amount without a named source
Says the audit was done without brand memory, or marks brand-dependent checks as not checked or provisional
